fix: `scrollable_viewport_chain` (tree/interaction.rs:432) builds and returns a full `Vec` of cloned controllers and physics for every scroll ancestor, and this helper runs once per focusable candidate in `directional_focus_target` (line 313), i.e. one allocation and a full chain walk per element per key press. Make the chain a lazy iterator, e.g. `fn scrollable_viewports(&self, element) -> impl Iterator<Item = (...)> + '_` walking `self.parent(..)`, then here use `self.scrollable_viewports(element).find(|(_, _, a, _, _)| *a == axis).map(|(owner, ..)| owner)`. Alternatively walk ancestors and return the first matching scroll render without cloning. The lazy iterator also removes the clones in `scroll_nearest_viewport`.

Only the nearest viewport is used, but the whole chain is allocated and cloned. Once `scrollable_viewport_chain` returns a lazy iterator (see the interaction.rs fix), use `let Some((_, controller, axis, reverse, _)) = self.scrollable_viewports(focused).next() else { return false; };`. Without that change, at minimum the chain can be built with `Vec::with_capacity`, but the lazy form is the real fix.

Finding the single focused keyboard element allocates and fills the whole focusable list (recursive walk plus flatten) only to scan it. Walk the tree without collecting, e.g. factor `focusable_elements_recursive` into a visitor that calls a closure per candidate and short-circuits, and use it here; or iterate `self.elements` and return the first `Gesture` whose `focus_node` has focus, provided the same reading-order result is preserved. Confirm the call frequency before changing; if it runs per frame, this is high severity.
